subject: Qualification: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations

Subject: Quick follow-up: deployment mode and data isolation (FinSecure)

Hi Emily —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned on the deployment/ security discussion: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for customer content and PKI/keys control.
- Regulatory note: data residency in us-east-1; long-term retention + audit log availability (7+ years) is required.
- Crypto: FinSecure wants customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) for encryption-at-rest and assurance that Redwood cannot access plaintext.
- Options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pools, Redwood-managed control plane), Private VPC / on-prem (customer-managed networking & control plane).

Questions you flagged for follow-up:
1) Difference between Dedicated vs Private VPC for data isolation and key control.
2) Whether logs and intermediate state (e.g., KV cache) are accessible to Redwood or persisted on shared storage.
3) Support for KMS/HSM integrations and proof points (SOC2 artifact, encryption whitepaper).

Suggested next steps:
- Schedule a 45m technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Dev Patel) to walk through infra diagrams, KMS/HSM options, and audit/log retention configs.
- I’ll attach a short one-pager that summarizes Dedicated vs Private VPC differences for your security & procurement teams.
- If you want procurement involved, loop them in and we can prepare draft terms.

Proposed times (PST): Tue 03/03 10:00-11:00 or Wed 03/04 09:00-10:00. Which works best for you / your team?

Attachments: finsecure-mrp-draft-ma-points.pdf (draft notes we referenced).

Thanks —

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: deployment mode and data isolation (FinSecure)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side before scheduling the deep-dive: 

1) Key management: FinSecure requires full control of encryption keys via an HSM-backed KMS. We need technical confirmation that customer-managed keys can be used for all persistent storage and that Redwood does not hold plaintext keys.

2) Compute tenancy: when you say “Dedicated capacity” — is that single-tenant compute and storage, or do we end up on shared storage/network fabrics with logical isolation? We need to understand whether any customer artifacts (logs, caches) are stored on multi-tenant infrastructure.

3) On-prem/air-gapped: this is a potential ask for certain regulated workloads — does Redwood support an on-prem bundle or fully air-gapped deployment? If so, what are the lead times and ops requirements?

4) Evidence: please share SOC2 / encryption whitepaper and any relevant diagrams we can pass to procurement (I’ve cc’d them).

If your one-pager can call out the differences specifically about tenancy, key custody, and log retention policies that will be helpful. We’re a little early in the procurement funnel but need these answers to classify the deployment mode.

Appreciate it —
Emily Zhao
Head of Cloud Security | FinSecure
emily.zhao@finsecure.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: emily.zhao@finsecure.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: deployment mode and data isolation (FinSecure)

Emily — thanks, good questions. High-level answers below; we’ll cover architecture and configs in the deep-dive. I’m available Tue 10:00 or Wed 09:00 — looks like Dev can join both.

1) Keys / KMS/HSM:
- Dedicated: supports customer BYOK via cloud KMS (customer project/account). We can integrate with your KMS so keys are customer-controlled and rotated on your schedule. Redwood does not retain plaintext keys; we only hold encrypted material necessary for routing.
- Private VPC / On-prem: supports direct HSM integration or local key material — you retain full custody. On-prem option gives you the highest assurance.

2) Compute & storage tenancy:
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools for inference (compute isolation). Storage may be in a customer-dedicated logical instance within our managed control plane; network and storage fabrics are logically isolated but still within Redwood’s managed infrastructure (no tenant co-mingling in compute).
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer-managed networking and storage; control plane can be customer-hosted which eliminates Redwood-managed storage. This is the recommended path if you require zero-management-plane data residency.

3) Logs / KV cache / intermediate state:
- By default, ephemeral caches (KV for model context) are kept in-memory per inference and not persisted. Persistent logs (audit, usage) are stored in a customer-dedicated project and can be exported to your logging stack. Retention windows are configurable; we can provide archival to your S3 or on-prem storage for long-term retention.

4) On-prem / air-gapped:
- We offer an on-prem package for regulated workloads; lead time typically 6-10 weeks depending on packaging and validation. Ops requirements: host spec (GPU/CPU), network ACLs for initial onboarding, and a maintenance window cadence. We’ll cover details in the call.

I’ve attached a short one-pager that summarizes Dedicated vs Private VPC which calls out the tenancy and key custody differences (attached).

Next step: propose we lock a 45m deep-dive w/ Dev (Solutions Eng) and Jordan (AE coverage). If procurement wants an intro before the technical call we can do a joint session.

Proposed times: Tue 03/03 10:00-10:45 PT or Wed 03/04 09:00-09:45 PT. Which do you prefer?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
